ny_st_nicks_wall.blurb: A small city bouldering spot in Harlem, on the edge of St. Nicholas Park in upper Manhattan. Fourteen problems are spread over four short sections along the sidewalk, on schist. Grades start at V0, where most of the problems sit, with a few around V3 and a single V4 at the top end, so it works for beginners and for a quick after-work session. The wall gets sun and is a short walk from the subway stops along St. Nicholas Avenue, which makes a car unnecessary.

ny_7_puzzle_palace.blurb: A short but steep, feature-rich wall in the Perched Ramparts section of the Powerlinez, in the Harriman area of southern New York. Most of the fourteen routes are set up as top-ropes, with two trad lines, and they run from very easy through the 5.8 and 5.9 range, topping out around 5.10. Holds and pockets on the face make repeated laps fun, and the steepness gives it a technical feel. Natural protection is sparse, so bring a long static rope for anchors. The scramble up to the base is steep and loose.

ny_potash_cliff.blurb: A small cliff in the Lake George part of the Adirondacks, split evenly between sport and trad lines. The fourteen routes begin around 5.8 and climb through the 5.11s into the low 5.12s, with a single route near 5.13. The wall looks south, so it catches sun through the day, though trees cast patches of shade. Belay spots are decent, and the holds are positive or follow cracks. The walk from the road is only a few minutes, which suits short days and a handful of hard pitches.

ny_frontiertown_crag.blurb: A compact Adirondack cliff in the Lake Champlain region, reached by a short uphill walk through woods from the road. Walls are steeper than they appear, which has made it a spot for hard sport routes in warm months, mostly in the 5.12 range with some 5.13, plus a few trad lines and one boulder problem. It also carries a couple of mixed lines and an ice route. It is a good choice for strong sport climbers looking for steep, powerful routes along the Northway corridor, rather than for beginners.

ny_right_wall.blurb: A bouldering wall on the right side of Lake Gulley, a ravine in Clark Reservation State Park near Syracuse. The buttress runs the length of the gulley and holds fourteen problems, nearly all between VB and V2, with a roughly even split of V0 and V2 climbs. That makes it a friendly place for beginners and intermediates building mileage. The area is mossy and still developing, so watch your footing and keep cleaning to a minimum. Reach it by walking the main trail from the parking lot past the playground, then turning left into the gulley.

ny_cliffs_minor.blurb: A set of small bouldering cliffs scattered around the First Overlook in the Grand Lake Reserve, in the north of New York State. The fourteen problems are all boulders and mostly easy to moderate, with about half at V1, a few at V0 or V2, and a handful of harder ones up to a V6 that is the area's standout. The setting is forested, with a small, fairly clean zone on the lowest tier. Expect a hike of roughly fifteen to twenty minutes from the lots to the overlook, then a short drop to the base on the left.
